purpose: Read-only check for overwhelming value-gradient dominance; not a training update or performance evaluation
method: Reconstruct four-frame screen stacks from the frozen model's own trace, padding initial history with the boot frame.
Compute frozen action log probabilities and values; use recorded visible-score rewards and visible life-loss/terminal events.
Calculate configured GAE in consecutive 256-action blocks with value bootstrap at block ends. Normalize advantages separately in each block.
Differentiate PPO actor loss minus entropy coefficient times entropy, and separately the actual weighted value loss (0.25 times mean squared return error).
Compare gradient norms and cosine over shared conv and hidden parameters. Compute the combined all-parameter norm and hypothetical 0.5 global clipping multiplier.
Do not call the optimizer. Check every model parameter remains byte-for-byte equal in its NumPy representation.
limitations: One selected best evaluation trajectory, not representative live training minibatches or an independent sample.
Single-trajectory blocks and per-block normalization differ from the learner's 32-worker rollout normalization and shuffled minibatches.
Uses the global-best checkpoint's GAE lambda 0.95, not the continuing learners' 0.99.
The final 20-action partial block is reported separately and excluded from the full-block ratio summary.
Does not prove a cause of the plateau or rule out value/policy interference. No optimizer or architecture change follows from this diagnostic alone.
